hypothesis.title: The Translation Layer
hypothesis.question: Does a transformation preserve more musical continuity when its intermediate representation is aligned with the relation that must survive?
hypothesis.hypothesis: If a musical transformation uses an intermediate representation aligned with the relation that must survive, then listeners will perceive stronger continuity than in a matched transformation using a representation that cuts across that relation.
hypothesis.rationaleMd: Bark-scale dynamics suggests that the frequency grid a processor hears through changes what it preserves perceptually [S2]. StreamMark shows that complex-domain audio structure can carry recoverable information through benign transformations while failing under identity-altering attacks [S3]. PHALAR reports that pitch-equivariance and phase-equivariance improve musical representation learning, and that phase-aware representations align with human coherence judgments [S4]. Score-understanding benchmarks show modality gaps between ABC and PDF score representations across onset, pitch, harmony, texture, and form [S5]. Speech-recognition fairness work shows that audio encoder design and compression quality can dominate downstream behavior and bias [S6]. Ice phase behavior adds the physical constraint: mathematically possible structures only matter when a path can actually reach them [S1].

recipe.title: Translation-Layer A/B
recipe.bodyMd: Build a 60-second source passage with drums, bass, chordal material, and one phase-sensitive or stereo-rich texture. Keep tempo, form length, key center, source motif, and integrated loudness constant. Render five transformations: Bark-band dynamics, arbitrary-band dynamics as a control grid, phase-preserved versus phase-disturbed translation, notation-codec translation from ABC and visual/staff or piano-roll forms, and a degraded front-end stress test using low bitrate, silence gaps, onset masking, or coarse pitch quantization [S1, S2, S3, S4, S5, S6]. The test asks whether continuity follows the representation that preserves the task-relevant relation rather than the version with the closest surface match.
dawChecklist: Create one 60-second source passage with drums, bass, chords, and a phase-sensitive texture.
Render a Bark-band dynamics version using 24 perceptual bands or the closest available approximation.
Render a matched arbitrary-band dynamics control with comparable loudness and gain reduction.
Render a phase-preserved timbral translation and a magnitude-preserved phase-disturbed control.
Translate a four-bar excerpt through two notation/workflow codecs, then compose one variation from each.
Render a degraded front-end version with low bitrate, silence gaps, onset masking, or coarse pitch quantization.
Loudness-match all versions and randomize playback order before listening.
Score each version for preserved density, phase coherence, motif, hierarchy, timing, accent, and harmonic path.

protocol.listeningContext: Studio monitors or neutral headphones, loudness-matched renders
protocol.listeningMethod: Blind randomized A/B comparison with written continuity notes

notes: Disconfirming evidence: listeners cannot distinguish representation-aligned transformations from surface-matched controls, or the preserved relation is only measurable in analysis and has no audible compositional consequence.
